name: room
text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text:
**Decision:** We will build every new package, tab enrichment, or draft element as a single, self-contained "module" that can be dropped into any project without extra setup.

**Why:** This keeps things simple and reusable. A module is easy to test, share, and slot into different tools, which speeds up our work and keeps quality high. It also makes it clear who made it—every module gets stamped "Created by EXCAVA," so credit is automatic.

**Trade-off:** We’re choosing flexibility over speed in some cases. A module might take a little longer to design upfront, but it pays off later when we reuse it or fix issues in one place. The alternative—quick, one-off tweaks—would clutter things and make future work harder.

name: Vet
text: **Pushback:** That’s a tidy idea, but modules can become a dumping ground for half-baked code if we don’t enforce strict boundaries. What if a module grows too big or does too much? Instead, we could split work into *tiny, single-purpose modules* (e.g., one for validation, one for UI) and only combine them when needed. To settle this, we’d need to see a concrete example of how a module would stay lean—and agree on a rule like “no module over 200 lines without a split.”
